standard.title: Plan, create and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations by experimenting with rhetorical devices, and the organisation and development of ideas, to engage audiences for different purposes in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create and deliver presentations developing ideas analytically and critically (AC9E9LY07). They have not yet planned, created, rehearsed and delivered presentations experimenting with rhetorical devices to engage audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations by experimenting with rhetorical devices, and the organisation and development of ideas, to engage audiences for different purposes.

nodes.label: Planning presentations with rhetorical awareness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a spoken or multimodal presentation that identifies purpose, audience and at least two rhetorical devices to be used, with a rationale.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plan for a spoken presentation that identifies purpose, audience, rhetorical devices to be used and how they will engage the audience.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a detailed plan for a spoken or multimodal presentation that organises and develops ideas for a specific purpose and audience, identifying rhetorical devices and explaining how they will engage the audience.
wider: Plan a persuasive presentation that manipulates rhetorical devices to compel the audience to act, explaining specifically how each device will achieve the intended response
Plan a panel discussion or debate on an issue related to a text, considering how the interactive format shapes rhetorical choices
Plan a reflective monologue as a character from a studied text, considering how character voice and rhetorical choices serve the narrative and analytical purpose
success_criteria: Identifies purpose and audience for the presentation
Names at least two rhetorical devices and explains how each will engage the audience

nodes.label: Creating and rehearsing the presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and rehearse a spoken or multimodal presentation, using rhetorical devices and refining delivery through rehearsal.
nodes.minimum_width: Create and rehearse a spoken presentation that uses at least two rhetorical devices, with evidence of rehearsal reflected in delivery.
nodes.typical_width: Create and rehearse a spoken or multimodal presentation that develops and organises ideas for a specific purpose, using rhetorical devices with evidence of deliberate preparation and rehearsal.
wider: Create a multimodal presentation that manipulates rhetorical devices across visual and spoken modes to compel the audience to act
Create and rehearse a reflective character monologue from a studied text, experimenting with how rhetorical choices support both characterisation and argument
Create a spoken text that incorporates the rhetorical strategies of First Nations Australian oratory or storytelling conventions
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 3 requires students to deliver the presentation — without sufficient rehearsal, the rhetorical choices planned and created cannot be executed effectively in real time and the delivery fails to achieve its purpose.

response_modes.reason: Delivery of rhetorical devices in real time requires rehearsal — students who have not practised sufficiently cannot execute their rhetorical choices effectively; rehearsal fluency is the threshold capability here.

success_criteria: Creates a presentation that includes at least two rhetorical devices
Shows evidence of rehearsal in the delivery — timing, delivery choices, responsiveness to audience

nodes.label: Delivering to engage the audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation that engages the audience for a specific purpose, using rhetorical devices effectively.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a spoken presentation that uses at least two rhetorical devices and demonstrates awareness of audience engagement.
nodes.typical_width: Deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation that engages the audience through effective use of rhetorical devices, appropriate organisation and clear development of ideas for a specific purpose.
wider: Deliver a persuasive multimodal presentation intended to compel the audience to act, using a range of rhetorical devices across spoken and visual modes
Participate in a debate or panel discussion about a text-related issue, using interaction skills and rhetorical devices to present and defend a position
Deliver a character reflective monologue that engages the audience through both rhetorical performance and analytical insight about the character's choices

response_modes.reason: Live delivery integrates planning, creation and rehearsal — students must coordinate rhetorical choices, organisational structure and audience responsiveness in real time; phase collapse here means the presentation fails to achieve its purpose despite adequate preparation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Debate, panel discussion and character monologue offer rich and varied delivery contexts — the challenge of adapting rhetorical choices to interactive formats (debate) is substantially more complex than single-speaker presentations.
success_criteria: Delivers a presentation that uses at least two rhetorical devices
Demonstrates audience engagement through at least one observable delivery choice (pacing, eye contact, rhetorical question, etc.)
